subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which principle does a stack follow?
explanation: A stack removes the most recently pushed item first.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which principle does a queue follow?
explanation: A queue removes the earliest enqueued item first.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What is the worst-case time complexity of linear search in n items?
explanation: Linear search may inspect all n items.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What does a singly linked-list node normally store besides data?
optionA: A pointer to the next node
explanation: Each singly linked node links to its successor.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What is the worst-case time complexity of merge sort?
explanation: Merge sort divides and merges in O(n log n) time.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What must a recursive function have to stop recursive calls?
explanation: A base case terminates recursion.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: In a binary search tree, values in the left subtree are normally…
optionB: always equal to the node key
explanation: A BST orders left-subtree keys below the node key.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which simple comparison sort repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order elements and has worst-case O(n²)?
explanation: Bubble sort compares and swaps adjacent elements; its worst case is quadratic.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What is a valid base case for factorial recursion?
explanation: The factorial definition uses 0! = 1 as a terminating base case.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which operation inserts a new item at the top of a stack?
explanation: Push adds an item to the top of a stack.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which queue operation removes the item at the front?
explanation: Dequeue removes the front item.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: What prerequisite does binary search require for a conventional array search?
explanation: Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search interval.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: If a node pointer is already known, inserting a node after it in a singly linked list takes what time?
explanation: The links can be changed in constant time when the insertion node is known.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: How is the next position commonly calculated in a circular array queue of capacity N? (variant 2)
explanation: Modulo wraps the index back to zero at the array boundary.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: In an inorder traversal of a binary tree, what is the visit order? (variant 2)
explanation: Inorder traversal visits left subtree, node, then right subtree.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: In a binary search tree, values in the left subtree are normally… (variant 2)
optionC: always equal to the node key
explanation: A BST orders left-subtree keys below the node key.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which sorting algorithm is generally stable and has worst-case O(n log n) time?
explanation: Merge sort has O(n log n) worst-case time and can be implemented stably.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which problem is commonly solved by divide-and-conquer recursion?
explanation: Merge sort recursively sorts subarrays and merges them.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: Which operation inserts a new item at the top of a stack? (variant 3)
explanation: Push adds an item to the top of a stack.

subject: Data Structures through C
text: In a standard queue, where is a new element inserted? (variant 3)
explanation: Enqueue inserts at the rear of a queue.
